NDT training in Orlando: how it works for Orlando employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Orlando employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT live online or onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight, to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Level I, II and III courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after formal training, documented experience, Level III-administered exams and a vision test. Atlantis has no classroom in Orlando. We bring the training to your crew.

Orlando's NDT market looks nothing like a Gulf Coast refinery town, and training has to reflect that. Central Florida's inspection work is built on four pillars. First, gas turbine engineering, manufacture and service, one of the largest concentrations of turbine expertise in the country. Second, defence and aerospace manufacturing. Third, the Space Coast, about an hour east, where launch providers, spacecraft builders and ground-systems contractors work around Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral. Fourth, a construction and infrastructure economy that keeps growing across the I-4 corridor. Power generation, airport MRO and the engineering teams behind the region's large theme-park attractions add further demand.

This section goes beyond the overview above. It covers per-method course content mapped to Central Florida work, the SNT-TC-1A path step by step, delivery options, Florida radiography requirements, and what Orlando NDT employers need from a written practice and a Level III. Request an Orlando training quote whenever you're ready.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Orlando

All courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and can be delivered to Orlando candidates as live online theory, onsite theory and practical at the employer's facility, or a blend. Your employer's written practice defines the required hours. See our training-requirements matrix for the reference figures.

MethodLevelsWhat Orlando employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, IIITurbine rotors, discs and castings, launch-structure and ground-support welds, and structural steel on construction projectsLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus documented UT experience
PAUT (phased array UT)II, IIIEncoded weld inspection on structural and pressure welds, and inspection of complex geometries on power and aerospace componentsUT Level II normally expected
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, IIIFlaw sizing in thick-section welds on power plant components and heavy structuresUT Level II normally expected
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, IIIWeld radiography on piping and pressure systems, and castings and assemblies in manufacturingFlorida radiographer requirements and radiation-safety training in addition to method training
MT (magnetic particle testing)I, IIFerromagnetic turbine and generator components at overhaul, structural and bridge welds, ride and attraction steel componentsLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus MT experience
PT (liquid penetrant testing)I, IIFluorescent inspection of turbine blades, vanes and combustion hardware; aerospace and space components; stainless and nickel alloysLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus PT experience
VT (visual testing)I, IIBorescope inspection of turbines, weld visual inspection on construction and fabrication, structural condition surveysLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus VT experience
ET (eddy current testing)I, IISurface-crack detection on turbine and aerospace components, conductivity testing, condenser and exchanger tubing at power plantsLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus ET experience

PT and ET for turbines. Gas turbine hardware is where Orlando's NDT work is most demanding. The penetrant course covers fluorescent systems, sensitivity levels, the effect of coatings and surface condition, process control and viewing conditions. The eddy current course covers impedance-plane analysis, surface and edge probes, conductivity and coating-thickness measurement, and crack detection on high-value parts. Technicians on turbine work must follow the OEM or customer procedure to the letter, so both courses stress procedure discipline alongside technique.

UT, PAUT and TOFD. The ultrasonic courses cover calibration, straight and angle beam, immersion principles, and evaluation of indications in forgings, castings and welds. Phased array and TOFD build on UT Level II for technicians moving into advanced weld inspection on power, launch and heavy structural work.

MT. The magnetic particle course covers magnetisation techniques, field verification, wet fluorescent inspection, demagnetisation and interpretation. It applies to generator and turbine steels at overhaul, structural and bridge welding, and the steel structures and mechanical components found in attraction engineering.

VT. The visual course covers direct and remote technique, including borescope inspection, which is a daily tool for turbine service technicians, and weld visual inspection for construction QA.

RT. The radiography course covers sources, exposure geometry, image quality indicators, and film and digital interpretation for welds and castings, alongside the Florida licensing requirements described below.

Level III. Orlando employers building their own certification programme can prepare a senior technician through ASNT Level III training, with readiness checks via UT Level II practice questions and the PAUT Level II mock exam.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Orlando, step by step

Under SNT-TC-1A your employer grants your certification according to its written practice. The steps are as follows.

  1. Employer written practice. Education, training, experience, examination, vision and recertification requirements for each method and level.
  2. Formal training. Classroom training in the method and level, online or onsite. The hours come from the written practice. See the training-requirements matrix.
  3. Documented experience. Supervised on-the-job hours in the method, recorded and signed.
  4. General exam. A written test of method principles.
  5. Specific exam. A written test on your employer's procedures, equipment and the specifications or OEM documents you work to.
  6. Practical exam. A hands-on exam on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified designee.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity is checked annually, with colour contrast differentiation as required.
  8. Certification. Your employer certifies you.
  9. Recertification. This happens at the interval your written practice defines.

A note for aerospace and space candidates: many aerospace manufacturers and their suppliers qualify NDT personnel to NAS 410, and some turbine and space customers impose their own qualification requirements. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only. Whether that training counts toward another programme is up to that programme's written practice and responsible Level III. For the full framework, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Orlando crews

  • Live online theory. Real-time classes with a Level III-led team, easy to fit around shift patterns at service shops, plants and manufacturing sites.
  • Onsite at your facility. Groups can be trained and examined at your shop, plant or site on your own equipment and representative parts. This matters most for turbine and aerospace work, where the parts and procedures are specific.
  • Blended. Online theory first, followed by a short onsite practical block.

We schedule around your operation: power-plant outage seasons, turbine shop workloads, launch campaigns on the Space Coast, and construction milestones. We also plan around Florida's hurricane season, when crews are often redeployed at short notice. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Orlando crew, or read how online NDT training works.

Where NDT technicians work in Orlando

Gas turbine engineering and service. Central Florida hosts major gas turbine engineering, service and repair operations. Blades, vanes, combustion hardware, rotors and casings are inspected at manufacture and at every overhaul, with PT, ET, UT, MT and VT all in demand under OEM procedures.

Defence and aerospace manufacturing. Orlando's defence electronics, missile and simulation industry includes precision manufacturing where NDT is part of quality assurance, typically under customer specifications and aerospace qualification requirements.

The Space Coast. Launch providers, spacecraft and satellite builders, and ground-systems contractors around Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station need NDT on launch structures, ground support equipment, cryogenic and high-pressure piping (ASME B31.3 is a common reference), pressure vessels and flight hardware. Many Orlando-based technicians commute east for this work.

Power generation. Central Florida's utility generating stations and combined-cycle plants need outage inspection of turbines, generators, boilers, heat recovery steam generators, piping and condensers.

Airport MRO and aviation. Orlando International and the region's other airports support maintenance operations using ET, PT, UT and VT under aircraft maintenance documentation.

Attractions engineering. The large theme parks maintain complex ride systems and steel structures. Engineering and maintenance teams, and their contractors, use MT, UT, PT and VT on structural welds, axles, wheel assemblies and other critical components.

Construction and infrastructure. The I-4 corridor's continuous construction, FDOT bridge programmes (AWS D1.5 for bridge welding) and structural steel buildings (AWS D1.1) create steady demand for VT, UT and MT in construction QA. After major storms, structural inspections of towers, signs and steel structures add short-notice work.

Radiography licensing in Florida. Florida is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is regulated by the Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Radiation Control, under state rules compatible with NRC's 10 CFR Part 34. Florida's rules require radiographers to complete formal training, supervised on-the-job training, and written and practical examinations, and to be certified by a recognised certifying entity. Radiographers moving to a new Florida licensee receive additional training on that licensee's operating and emergency procedures. Atlantis teaches the RT method. Licensing and radiation safety remain the employer's responsibility.

What Orlando employers typically ask for. Turbine and aerospace employers want PT and ET Level II with strict procedure discipline, and often an aerospace-specific qualification. Construction and power employers want UT, MT and VT Level II with clean records. Some clients also require credentials such as NAS 410 qualification or AWS CWI. Those are separate schemes, and Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only.

Level III services and written practices for Orlando NDT companies

Orlando NDT companies often serve customers with very different expectations: a turbine OEM on Monday, a construction GC on Tuesday, a launch-site contractor on Wednesday. Each customer audits against its own requirements, and a generic written practice rarely survives all of them.

Atlantis supports Orlando employers with:

  • Written-practice development and review. SNT-TC-1A written practices tailored to your methods, levels and customer base, with notes on where specific customers invoke additional qualification requirements.
  • Outsourced Level III services. Exam administration, procedure review and approval, and certification file audits.
  • Corporate programmes. Structured multi-method training plans for growing inspection teams.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance. Practical interpretation for your scope.

Book a Level III consultation for your Orlando programme.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in five environments, including an aircraft hangar, an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Orlando trainees on turbine, aerospace and construction tracks can walk through technique and set-up before handling real equipment.

It is practice only. The simulator does not replace hands-on training, and it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens that SNT-TC-1A requires.

Your instructor

Programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets course content, oversees practical training and examinations, and leads written-practice and Level III work for Atlantis clients. Orlando employers work directly with a Level III.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Orlando

How do I get NDT certified in Orlando?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, you complete formal training in a method, build documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice. Atlantis delivers the training online or onsite.

Can I take NDT training online in Florida?

Yes, for the theory. Atlantis runs live online classes for Level I, II and III theory in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Practical training and the practical exam must be done in person on real specimens. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Your employer's written practice sets both classroom hours and documented experience for Level I and Level II. The experience part usually takes longest. See the reference figures in our training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Florida?

The employer needs a licence or registration from the Florida Department of Health's Bureau of Radiation Control. Radiographers must complete the state's training, on-the-job training and examination requirements and be certified by a recognised certifying entity. SNT-TC-1A RT method certification is separate.

What does NDT training cost in Orlando?

We don't publish prices. Quotes depend on method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery, and any written-practice or Level III support. You'll receive a cohort or onsite quote within one business day. Request an Orlando training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Orlando employers?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used by power, construction and industrial employers. Aerospace, space and some turbine customers may require NAS 410 or their own qualification, for which SNT-TC-1A training is a foundation but not a replacement. Each employer certifies you under its own programme.

Can I work on the Space Coast with SNT-TC-1A certification?

Many ground-systems and construction roles use SNT-TC-1A. Flight hardware and some aerospace customers often require NAS 410 or customer-specific qualification. Check each role's stated requirements.

Which NDT method should I learn first in Orlando?

For turbine and aerospace work, PT and ET. For construction and power, VT, MT and UT. UT gives the broadest options across sectors.

Can Atlantis train our Orlando crew onsite?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility, on your own equipment and parts, is the standard model for groups. Ask about onsite training for your Orlando crew.

Does my certification transfer when I change employers?

No. SNT-TC-1A certifications belong to the issuing employer. Your training, experience and exam records move with you and support re-certification by your new employer.

What is the difference between Level II and Level III?

A Level II performs, interprets and reports examinations. A Level III establishes procedures, interprets codes, and trains and examines Level I and II personnel. See ASNT Level III training.

Can I practise before my practical exam?

Yes. The Practical NDT simulator offers 12 methods in five environments. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam.

Where can I read about NDT pay in Florida?

We don't publish local salary figures. Our NDT salary guide explains the factors that drive pay.
